courseName: [ENG 101 Section 119] English for Academic Purposes I
title: Attractive Cities Activity
content:
Activity: What Makes a City Livable, Attractive, and Functional?
Look at the list of city features below.
1. Decide which features are absolutely necessary for a livable, attractive, and functional city, and which ones could
be eliminated.
2. From the “necessary” features, choose 5 key features that you believe make the biggest difference to people’s
lives.
3. Be ready to explain your choices to the class.
A Livable / Attractive / Functional City:
Feature Necessary Can Be Eliminated
has short walking distance to
schools/hospitals/shopping areas
has squares and public places (e.g. parks)
closed for vehicular traffic
has bicycle lanes
has green areas
offers gatherings/activities to encourage
community spirit
offers mixed housing (people of different
ages, races, and income levels can live close)
depends on ecologically sustainable energies
provides effective public transportation
has shopping streets/centers
has vibrant city life – with people on its
streets, including the elderly and the disabled
has entertainment opportunities: open fields,
nearby forests
offers cultural entertainment: museums,
theatres, cinemas, etc.
has good schools, universities, and hospitals
values the history of the city/region
has high economic activity, providing goods,
services, and jobs
has beautiful streets with beautiful
houses/buildings to look at
ensures public safety (well-lit streets, low
crime rates, safe crossings)
is affordable to live in (housing and services
within reach for most residents)
is accessible for everyone (including the
elderly and people with disabilities)
has clean air and water (environmental
protection and waste management)
has reliable infrastructure (electricity,
internet, water, sanitation)
prepares for emergencies and natural
disasters (floods, earthquakes, etc.)
